statement: Nvidia's long-term supply commitments rose to $279 billion over the next few years, up from $119 billion three months earlier, with $92 billion due in the remainder of fiscal 2027 and $87 billion and $88 billion across fiscal 2028 and 2029.
why: More than doubling committed purchase obligations in one quarter is a hard financial signal that the vendor is locking in components for a much larger build plan.

impact.mechanism: Binding supply commitments reserve memory and manufacturing capacity ahead of shipment, pulling forward orders across the upstream chain.

evidence.excerpt: $279 billion on supply commitments over the next few years -- up from $119 billion only three months earlier
$92 billion is due in the remainder of fiscal 2027, followed by $87 billion and $88 billion across fiscal 2028 and 2029.

confidence.basis: Secondary outlet summarizing figures that originate in Nvidia's filing; the filing itself is not the fetched document.
